ORAL ANSWERS TO QUESTIONS 
Misappropriation of funds by NGOs 
*161. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS 
AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) the specific reasons for which large number of NGOs, etc. have  
not submitted utilization certificates vide Ministry's Annual Report for the year  
2006-07; 
(b) whether any special efforts have been made to recover the amount running into 
hundreds of crores remaining un-accounted for years; 
(c) whether Government have considered to file criminal cases against the defaulting 
parties for breach of trust and misappropriation of Government funds; 
(d) whether the involvement of Ministry's officials in financial bungling has been 
investigated; and 
(e) if so, the results thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR): 
(a) to (e) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (e) The matter of a very large number of pending Utilization Certificates (UCs) has 
received due attention in the Ministry and concerted efforts have been made for liquidating 
the pending UCs. As a result, the number of UCs which stood at 10,576 amounting to Rs. 
1233.4 crores in March, 2005 has been reduced to 7,235 UCs amounting to Rs. 143.72 
crores in August, 2007. 
The examination of the pending UCs reveals that the Ministry provides grants to a 
very large number of NGOs, based at the field level. They have limited capacity in terms 
of accounting procedure, documentation, and preparation of reports, etc. They have to 
seek assistance from others, including certif ied chartered accountants, to prepare the 
necessary documentation resulting in delay in the submission of the UCs. Further, a large 
numbers of educational institutions have 

2      Oral Answers [RAJYA SABHA] to Questions 
been given grants for developing sports infrastructure. The scheme has since been transferred 
to the State Governments and the UCs pertaining to these institutions are taken up in the 
Ministry. 
The Ministry has also initiated serious discussions with the National Sports Federations 
for streamlining the procedure for grants and reducing the number of pending UCs. The 
grants-in-aid schemes for NGOs for youth and adolescents have been streamlined in 2005-06 
providing a greater role to State Governments in terms of scrutiny, pre -appraisal and 
prioritization of NGO proposals for consideration by the Ministry. With effect from the 
current financial year, the transfer of funds through the electronic clearance system has 
been adopted and the sanctions are posted in the Ministry's website as well. 
The Ministry has also launched a drive to reconcile the UCs in respect of grantee 
institution and NGO, who have received funds under the different scheme, of the Ministry 
in the past so as to enable the Ministry to arrive at the final position of pending UCs.  
As regards legal action, Rule 209/211 of the General Financial Rules (GFR) provides 
that where the UC is not received from the grantee within the prescribed time, the Ministry 
or Department will be at liberty to blacklist such Institution or Organization from any future 
grant, subsidy or other type of financial support from the Government. This fact should also 
be put on the website. In accordance with the provisions contained in GFR, no grants are 
released to any NGO against whom UC is pending except under exceptional circumstances 
such as sending a national team abroad. However, in such exceptional cases, adequate 
precautions are taken to ensure that funds are used prudently and strictly in accordance 
with the conditions laid down by the Ministry. Further , the list of black-listed NGOs has 
been placed on the website of the Ministry. 
The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) have investigated a complaint against some 
officials of the Ministry regarding their possible involvement in processing cases relating to 
grants to NGOs. After investigation, the Commission did not find any serious violation in 
the matter. 
SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Sir, on a reading of the Annual Report of the 
Ministry, we see that the problem of non-compliance of utilization certificates seems quite 
serious. There is an amount of almost Rs. 251 crores shown in the Annual Report with 
UCs outstanding from various NGOs and Organisations. The most worrying about this is 
that over Rs. 90 crores out of these relate to the last few years, that is, from 2003 onwards. 
Further there is only one paragraph on the subject in the Annual Report which states, 
"Grants have been stopped to such organisations that have failed to submit the UCs." And I 
believe this is hardly any solution. Sir, my first supplementary to the hon. Minister is: What 
are the criteria which the Ministry follows for grants to NGOs and in selecting these NGOs? 
Also, can an individual, behind a defaulting NGO, apply for and receive grants through 
another NGO? 
SHRI MAN1 SHANKAR AIYAR: Sir, we were under very strict instructions from the 
Ministry of Finance to totally deny any form of additional monies from the Government to 
NGOs whose pending UCs had not been cleared. But because we 

Oral Answers [23 AUG, 2007] to Questions      3 
settle down in a really significant way to clearing these pending utilisation certificates 
by obtaining as many as we could, and where there were certain differences of view 
between the Pay and Accounts Officer on the one hand and our own Ministry on the 
other in respect of information that had been supplied or not supplied, we have had very 
significant success as indicated in the answer itself to reducing, in terms of value, the 
number of these pending U.C.s. We brought it down from over Rs. 1200 crores in 
March, 2005, to Rs. 143 crores as of this month. But the numbers have not reduced 
significantly. The numbers have only gone down from about 10,500 to a little over 
7,000. This clearly shows that we have succeeded in settling the large value pending 
U.C.s. But because the U.C.s pending go back to 1985, and many of them are very small 
value U.C.s, the process of getting it all cleared in respect of each one of them is a time-
consuming one. But I think we can claim the credit for having made a very, very 
significant progress. Now in the light of this very significant progress that we did 
succeed in making, we succeeded in getting from the Ministry of Finance permission to 
start releasing grants, where there were special circumstances in 2006 such as the Doha 
Asian Ga mes, and we have also succeeded in securing a distinction between those 
NGOs which have pending U.C.s after 2000 and those pending U.C.s before 2000. In 
cases where we succeeded in clearing the post -2000 U.C.s, we have been releasing 
grants. But for the pr e-2000 U.C.s, we are still checking things out, and the 
improvement with regard to NSFs is, I think, something that we should draw attention 
to. When we started this exercise, every one of the 65 National Sports Federations had 
pending U.C.s. We have now r eached a stage where 34 of these 65 have no pending 
U.C.s and 19 of them have no pending U.C.s after 2000. So, there are only 12 National 
Sports Federations who have pending U.C.s both pre and post -2000, some of which are 
under dispute. So, I think, we can say that systematically we are making a very 
significant progress. The NSFs and the 10A, in particular, do object to delays that take 
place in the release of grants to them. But there has been such massive financial 
impropriety, if not corruption, in the past that clearing up all that and compelling them to 
come on line has resulted in a certain element of dissatisfaction. But I think the House 
will agree with me that it is desirable that we should have financial propriety with 
respect to all NGOs includin g the National Sports Federation and the Indian Olympics 
Association. 
SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Sir, my second supplementary is a question 
of a broader issue of principles. Does the Minister not think that the current regime of 
FCRA that regulates foreign donations to a number of genuine NGOs and makes it very 
difficult, should be re -examined given the fact that we have a number of NGOs, as we 
can see from the UCs, that are not complying when there are domestic donations?  
SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR: Sir, the question of FCRA and its application 
would have to be referred to the hon. Minister of Home Affairs. 
SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKAR REDDY: Sir, as far as the money released to 
NGOs is concerned, there is no mechanism of cross -verification at the district or the  
State level. You have a mechanism in rural development called the Vigilance and 
Monitoring Committee headed by the local MP, and all the local representatives are 
members of that body.  I would like to know whether the 

4       Oral Answers [RAJYASABHA] to Questions 
Minister is willing to refer all such matters to a body at the district level or the State 
level so that there can be cross-verification. 
SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR: Sir, the hon. Member is right that till some time ago there 
was no kind of checking by the State Government and we did discover, therefore, that we did 
have serious problems with regard to a large number of these NGOs. So, we have now put in 
place a system whereby the NGOs' viability, the NGOs' sincerity, the fact that it exists, are 
certified to us by the State Government before we take up these proposals. And since this 
procedure has been in operation only for a little over an year, I don't think it is yet time to 
evaluate. But if in evaluation we discover that a further check by the Central Government 
or through a Central agency at the State level is required, we can certainly do so. But I 
believe that if State Governments are responsible in this regard, then we will find it. 
The other point that I would like to make, especially becau se I do see that the Prime 
Minister is here, is that the Rural Development Ministry gets such large sums of money 
that it is well worth setting up a District Vigilance and Monitoring Committee. But we, in 
Youth Affairs and Sports, are much less well-endowed. So, perhaps, it is well worth putting up 
a District Monitoring Committee to look at the small sums of money that we are entitled to 
disburse. 
SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN NAIK: Sir, most of these NGOs are registered under a 
very scanty, old legislation called the Societies Registration Act of 1860 in which there are no 
provisions for accountability and any NGO can behave in any manner because the Act is 
very old. When crores of rupees of the Government money are allotted through the NGOs 
which are registered under such an old Act, I would like to know whether the Government 
will propose to bring for vard a new exhaustive legislation to register, with detailed 
provisions pertaining to accountability, registration, etc. 
SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR: Sir, the Societies Act like many other Acts has a date 
that goes back to the 19th century. But several of these have been amended over time and 
even after our Constitution came into force. So, it is entirely possible to make changes in the 
Societies Act to meet the kind of objectives that the hon. Member has in mind. But it is not 
my Ministry that would deal with the Act as a whole. We can only take the Act as 
prepared by the Ministry concerned and implement it in our Ministry. 
SHRI VEDPRAKASH P. GOYAL: Sir, my question to th e hon. Minister is whether, 
for general awareness of the people and for the information of all Members of Parliament 
in both the Houses, he is going to publish a statement State -wise how much was the 
allocation, to which NGOs, who are the defaulters and, a s has been asked in the main 
question, what actual action has been taken against the defaulters. 
SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR: Sir, my Ministry would have no difficulty in furnishing 
this information to the hon. Member or, indeed, to all the Members. I have the  
information, in fact, with me here. But clearly the time of the House cannot be taken in 
my reading it out here. But we will furnish this information and, if the Chair so directs, we 
can give it to all Members of Parliament; otherwise, I will

question later. 
SHRI S. S. AHLUWALIA: Sir, it will be more convenient if he puts it on the net.  
MR. CHAIRMAN: Next question. 
SHRI MA NI SHANKAR AIYAR: Sir, may I just answer him to say that we will 
certainly put it on the website and therefore, anybody could access it there. But I will 
send it directly to the hon. Member who asked the supplementary. 
Floors allowed under Master Plan 2021 
*162. SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI: Will the Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of floors (excluding Ground Floor) which have been allowed in 
the Master Plan 2021 in the houses constructed before 1st January, 2007; 
(b) if those houses  have any additional floors, whether Government are  
considering to regularize those floors by accepting penalty charges; and 
    (c) whether  Government are  also  considering regularization of Hanging Projections 
of those houses by charging penalty amount? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT (SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY): (a) to 
(c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha 
Statement 
(a) and (b) The Master Plan for Delhi (MPD) -2021, notified on 7.2.2007, inter alia, 
prescribes the Development Control Norms for buildings in residential plotted housing 
in respect of maximum ground coverage. Floor Area Ratio (FAR) and number of 
dwelling units for different size of plots. MPD 2021 also prescribes the maximum height 
of the building in residential plotted housing as 1 5 metres. Permissible ground coverage 
and FAR subject to fulfillment of other terms and conditions including maximum height 
of 15 metres will determine the number of floors which can be constructed on a given 
size of plot. As per the terms and conditions l aid down, plot owners/allottees seeking 
regularization of construction in terms of additional coverage/additional height are 
required to pay a penalty, compounding charges and betterment levy or additional FAR 
chaiges as well as special compounding charges  at the rates notified by Government for 
this purpose. However, this is subject to orders of the Supreme Court. 
(c) As for hanging projections, the Delhi Building Bye -Laws, permit certain  
types of projections into open spaces such as cornice, chajja, weath er shade,  
canopy, balcony and certain types of cantilever strictly within the individual plot.  
Projections on public land are not permitted. 
SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI: Sir, two parts, namely, (a) and (b) of my question have 
been replied together by the Jon. Minis ter. I went through the answer given by the hon. 
Minister, and, unfortunately, I found that my main question has not been replied by the 
hon. Minister. The main question was, 'if those houses have any additional floors, 
whether Government are considering to regularise those 

6       Oral Answers [RAJYA SABHA] to Questions 
floors by accepting penalty charges'. This question has not been replied by the hon. 
Minister. Sir, in his reply, the hon. Minister has mentioned about the rules and regulations. He 
has al so mentioned that those structures prior to 2007, their floor area/ratio was also 
considered —  the area was considered — and the rules have been framed. But, 
unfortunately, the court had issued some specific directions in the matter relating to these 
structures. The only reference is made at the end of the reply by stating, "however, this is 
subject to the orders of the Supreme Court." Sir, I would like to know from the hon. 
Minister whether all these structures beyond ground floor will be regularized in Delhi and 
whether the Government is ready to make necessary changes in the Act for doing so. 
SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY: Sir, the hon. Member has not only been a Chief Minister, 
but he has also vast experience in the Corporation of Mumbai. Sir, I want him to appreciate 
that the floors as such are not mentioned in Master Plans. Floors flow out of three critical 
variables. One is, maximum ground coverage, the other is FAR, Floor Area Ratio, which in 
some parts of the country is called FSI and the height. Therefore, I  could not answer the 
question in terms of floors. However, if you go by MPD 2001, in generality of cases what 
was permitted was ground plus two. Since we went in for liberalized norms under the 
Master Plan 2021, we can have ground plus three. However, thi s can be availed of 
provided concerned people pay penalty charges, compounding charges and so on and so 
forth. Therefore, Sir, I could not answer the question in terms of floors. He asked me as to 
what the Supreme Court orders mean. The Supreme Court is co nsidering the Master Plan 
Document as a whole. However, it did pass some interim orders. They said the new 
liberalized norms in respect of additional accommodation will not come into force. Later, 
they partly revised those norms. We are keen to see that most of the constructions that 
have taken place are regularized. I am of the considered view maximum area already 
constructed has been sought to be regularized in the MPD 2021. 
SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI: Sir, from the answer given by the hon. Minister, I presume 
that the Government has decided to regularise, as he said, 'maximum'. Sir, the word 
'maximum' does not give exact meaning because there are lakhs of people who are staying 
on first floors and second floors in Delhi. May I presume that their structures will b e 
regularized? I also want to know whether the projections, excepting those which have 
become hindrance to the road or some projections which are on the Government plan, 
excepting those, all other projections will be regularized. 
SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY: Sir, when I say maximum, I mean overwhelming number of cases. 
If somebody had built four floors instead of three, we are regularising. If somebody had built 
six, I would not be able to do that because if all others who did not build begin to do that, 
it would be a burden on the infra structural services. I should regularize keeping in mind 
the ability to provide infrastructure services. 
As far as hanging projections, we do permit regularisation of hanging projections so 
long as they do not trespass upon public land. Public land, the hon. Member would kindly 
appreciate, is a sacred thing and public land is meant for common use. If the hanging 
projections do not encroach upon public land, we are prepared to regularize them.

Unwanted tele-marketing calls 
*163. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA RAO: Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS 
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether TRAI has put in place norms to ensure that tele- marketeers do not 
disturb phone users; 
(b) to what extent the National Do Not Call (NDNC) Registry would  help poorer 
sections to get access to it and ensure that they are not disturbed; 
(c) whether it is a fact that poorer people would not be able to properly avail of the 
'National Registry'; 
(d) the steps proposed to evolve a Registry with a positive list of su bscribers 
who welcome telemarketing; and 
(e) the steps to protect people from unwanted SMS messages? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND 
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a) to (e) A Statement is 
laid on the Table of the   House. 
Statement 
(a) Yes, Sir. TRAI has issued regulation on Unsolicited Commercial  
Communication on 5th June, 2007. 
(b) and (c) NDNC Registry has been put in place to register requests of mobile  
subscribers who does not want to be disturbed by tele -marketing calls. This  
registry does not discriminate between poor and rich. Any mobile subscriber can  
request his/her own service provider to get his number included in NDNC registry.  
This facility is free of cost for the subscribers. 
(d) There is no proposal to evolve a registry with a positive list of subscriber who 
welcome tele-marketing calls. 

10     Oral Answers [RAJYA SABHA] to Questions 
(e) The scheme of NDNC registry is applicable for unwanted tele -marketing SMS 
messages also. 
SHRI V. HANUMANTHA RAO: Mr. Chairman, Sir, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of 
India had been set up to regulate the telecom companies. But it seems that the main job of 
TRAI is only to help private telecom companies. I have never seen an action taken by TRAI 
whereby it protects the public. Unless there is a lot of media out cry, the TRAI never acts 
to protect the public. It is not only in the matter of tele-marketing that TRAI is not doing 
its job but also in the matter of price of phone calls whereby the prices of SMS and every 
other subject, TRAI never does anything to protect the interest of the public. My first 
supplementary is whether the Government will make the Registry different so that all tele-
marketing is banned unless the subscriber registers for tele-marketing. How will the TRAI 
make sure that the public is not harassed just to enable telecom companies to make more 
money and how would poor people be protected who are disturbed constantly by 
unwanted phone calls? 
DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD: Sir, this question is relating to unsol icited telemarketing 
calls. The TRAI has issued a Notification dated 5th June, 2007. The Department of Telecom 
has directed all the telecom operators to register tele-marketeers and also asked the NIC of 
the IT Department to prepare software and make a Registry. Every telemarketeer should 
register first with that Registry and then a telephone subscriber can call has or her service 
provider to register himself or herself with the Registry by saying that he does not want 
to receive any unsolicited tele-marketing calls. If the telemarketeer makes a call to that 
number, then he will be charged Rs. 500 per call. So, the TRAI is doing its best for the 
development of telecom sector. Sir, TRAI, as a regulator, is doing its job. I, on behalf of 
the Telecom Ministry, can say with confidence that the TRAI is doing its work satisfactorily. 
SHRI V. HANUMANTHA RAO: Sir, part (a) of my second supplementary is this What 
steps will the Government take to make the TRAI pro -active and regulate the telecom 
companies? The telecom companies are financial giants and everyone is afraid of them. So, 
what steps will the Government take to appoint strong and independent Members in 
TRAI? 
Part (b) is: Instead of having a Do -Not-Call-Registry, which is friendly to telecom 
companies, what must have been arranged by the Government is to have a Permitted-Call-
Registry. Sir, Do -Not-Call- Registry will only help the telecom companies. We must 
remember that in the recent New Seven Wonders of the World contest only the telecom 
companies have gained millions of dollars. Is it not true? The hon. Minister may give a 
reply. 
DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD: Sir, the TRAI has issued an advertisement in almost all the 
major newspapers of the country asking tele -marketeers to register themselves by 31st 
August, 2007. O therwise, their telephones will be disconnected if they make any tele-
marketing calls. Most likely, from 5th September, 2007, there

will be a Registry for subscribers to register himself or herself with his or her telecom 
operator and register the name and number by saying that they do not want to receive 
any unsolicited tele-marketing calls. So, Sir, TRAI has taken the lead in it. Of course, we 
have received complaints from the subscribers and that is why th e TRAI and the 
Government, in tandem, are doing this work. 
DR. K. MALAISAMY: I wish the hon. Chairman generous to me every time. 
Sir, when a facility is given to avoid any disturbance, it is most welcome. I would like 
to know from the hon. Minister whether such facilities and services are really reaching the 
subscriber, particularly when the norms warrant that your services should be timely, 
equal, continuous and adequate. These are the norms under which you are functioning. 
But the general complaint is tha t it does not reach the subscriber at all. If that is the case, 
what are the measures take by the Department? And, whether such measures are adequate 
and effective? 
DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD: Sir, as I said in my reply, this facility will start most likely

themselves by 31st August, 2007. So, even after that, as I said earlier, if a telemarketeer calls 
somebody who is registered himself or herself with the NDNC Registry, then, that 
telemarketeer will be charged a tariff of Rs. 500 per call. By doing these types of  things, 
the Department, in collaboration with the TRAI, is trying to get rid of unsolicited calls 
received by common subscriber from tele-marketeers. Sir, SMS is also included in this. 
SHRI R. SHUNMUGASUNDARAM: Sir, sometimes when we get calls from tele-marketeers 
full numbers are not displayed, only four or five digits are displayed. Further, when we 
attend to the call, we hear the recorded computerised voices. This happens w hen we are 
on roaming also. Thus, we are compelled to pay for those services that we don't require, 
that we don't solicit for. Will the Ministry take into consideration deducting those calls 
and instead charge for them from those companies which make unsolicited calls? 
DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD: Yes, Sir. The entire motive of the Department and the TRAI is to 
save the telephone subscribers from the unsolicited telemarketing calls. This is the first step 
we are taking. As soon as we will be able to do this and if ot her things emerge and the 
Department feels technically that we need something extra to do, the Government will do 
everything on its part to give concessions and to redress the grievances of the subscribers

SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Sir, I would like to know from the hon. Minister whether 
there is any timeframe prescribed that the mobile number which do not receive any 
telemarketing calls has to be there on NDNC registry. If yes, what is the period of 
mandated time that the mobile numbers hav e to be there on the registry? I would also like 
to know whether it is true that NDNC registry is only for personal phone numbers and 
business-to-business calls are not covered by the registry. Also, how long the personal 
phone numbers will remain on the registry?

NDNC registry, it will be valid for ten years. As far as business -to-business calls are

phone to that number from any number, then, they will be charged as per the tariff. I

SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE: Sir, the hon. Member is fully aware that the quota is 
determined not by the Government, b ut it is determined by the Government of His 
Majesty, the Government of Saudi Arabia. And, the formula which they follow is, per one 
million population, I mean per one million Muslim population of a country, they give a 
quota of 1,000 pilgrims. In that context, as per India's Muslim population, which as per the 
Census Report is around 147 million, we are entitled to have a quota— as per the formula of 
the Royal Government of Saudi Arabia —  of 1,47,000. Last year, the Royal Government of 
Saudi Arabia was gracious enough to give an additional quota of 10,000. This year also, 
they have given this additional quota. That means, a quota of 1,57,000 will be available to 
us out of which 1,10,000 will be routed through the Haj Committee and 47,000 will be 
operated through the private tour operators. 
Therefore, we do not have any intention of reducing it, rather we try to get more 
because, for instance, against the quota of 1,57,000 which is available to us,

SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE: Most respectfully, Sir, I would like to submit that as I 
mentioned, as per the practices, which we follow all over the year, that for 100,000 
pilgrims, —  this year, it is 110,000; for phase II in 2006, it was 1,10,000 — recommendations 
are made by the State Haj Committees. Now, every day, we receive requests from the hon. 
Members. Now, if we fix the quota, i.e., two recommendations for each M.P., that means, 
543+245=788 M.Ps., I don't think that it would be very fair. But so far as the 
recommendations of Members of Parliament are concerned, we give utmost consideration to 
them. Most of the Members' recommendations are being put into effect; and we accept them. 
But it would be difficult for me to fix some sort of quota distribution because there are a 
large number of MPs who are not concerned —  I want to say with due respect —  if it was 
confined only to minority or Muslim MPs. But I am afraid, as Members of Parliament, we 
cannot make such a discrimination. So, these things have serious implications. My colleague 
here is flooded with such requests from everywhere. Some of th em are from his 
constituencies. A majority of Members have their constituencies. I myself represent the 
second largest Muslim -populated constituency in India. which is next only to Mr. E. 
Ahammed's constituency, according to the Census Report. Therefore, I am fully aware of 
the sensitivity of this issue. My colleague is looking into it. Please don't insist upon fixing 
a quota. As far as possible, we will try to accommodate the recommendations of the 
Members of Parliament. ...(Interruption)... 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Dr. Gill, please. 
DR. M.S. GILL: Sir, my question is not just to the hon. Minister, but it is also for the 
entire House. It is a fundamental question of national State policy. What is the policy on 
subsidising and assisting religious pilgrimage in this cou ntry as per the secular 
Constitution given by Nehru and Ambedkar? That is the first question to be answered. 
The second point is, about equal treatment to all people. ...(Interruption)... Please, I don't 
need help. It is about equal treatment to all citize ns of this country, on whatever policy is 
being made. It is not today's policy; it existed even before and we all know it. 
Sir, my question to the hon. Minister is would he first kindly get this matter resolved 
even from the Supreme Court, at the earliest possible so that we know what is the ultimate 
law of this country? Secondly, in the meanwhile, as the policy is being followed, will the 
Minister also agree to it that Christians and Jews be sent in a similar fashion by air to 
Jerusalem, that Sikhs do not suffer on trains and 

Oral Answers [23 AUG, 2007] to Questions    21 
buses and paying Rs. 1100 for 30 miles and be sent by air to Nanakana Sahib and Islamabad 
and that even the majority of this country is not sent to Mansarovar, via Dharchula, to die on 
the way, but sent via Beijing as well as via Kathmandu and Lhasa by air? 
SHPI PRANAB MUKHERJEE: Sir, so far as the first part of the hon. Member's question is 
concerned, 1 am afraid the issue is very important and sensitive and we could have a 
discussion on this. Unfortunately, it is not meant for Question Hour. As per your directions 
and your predecessors' directions, it is strictly prohibited to take up policy matters for 
discussion during Question Hour as the time is very limited. The issue could be discussed 
and debated upon; I have no problems with that. So, I cannot respond to the question on a 
policy matter. 
Secondly, it is not possible for me to give any assurance on what view the Supreme 
Court would take. But Government's views will be submitted, as they have already been 
submitted along with the Special Leave Petition through an affidavit. 
As far as the third aspect of it is concerned, I do agree and we do provide specific 
instructions in respect of the progress of two pilgrimages. A large number of pilgrims visit 
shrines located in Pakistan. Even this very morning, I received notices in the other House 
in respect of one particular shrine which has been occupied by unauthorised persons and 
where pilgrims are not able to even come out of the shrine. We are looking into these 
matters. We shall try to see that as far as possible we provide assistance to pilgrims. We do 
provide some support to Mansarovar pilgrims —  the pilgrimage that is being conducted by 
the Ministry of External Affairs —  as permissible within the existing policy. I shall not make 
any comparison between this pilgrimage and that. We also provide some support to the Sikh 
pilgrims, not in terms of money, but in terms of logistics support such as making 
arrangements for them. But these are all larger issues and I would be too glad to share my 
perception and listen to the perception of hon. Members through a structured debate. I 
have no problems with that.

SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE: Sir, surely I do not have the liberty of divulging the 
decisions of the Cabinet which were not made public. So far as this question is concerned, 
subsidy is not merely in one area. Subsidies in large areas are being reviewed from the broad 
economic point of view, but not from this viewpoint that subsidy is given to a particular 
purpose or a particular pilgrimage and, therefore, it should be reduced; We do not subscribe 
to that type of view. Yes, one can appreciate overall re duction of subsidy to facilitate and 
to have a better fiscal management. The approach should not be to reduce the 'X' or 'Y' 
subsidy of Haj pilgrimage. 
The second point is that subsidies are increasing not only because the number of 
pilgrims are increasing or the cost of operation is increasing or the cost of air travel is 
increasing. Since 1995, Haj pilgrimage through ships is abandoned. All of them are being 
transported in a specific period of time through airlines. A lot of logistic arrangements 
have to be made. We require during a particular period of time a large number of aircrafts 
which are not available. So, we are helping through Air India and Indian Airlines. They are 
put into operation and they are doing their best. The cost is also increasing sub stantially 
from year to year apart from the number of piigrims, which are increasing year to year.

Statement 
Details of major findings of the Court of Inquiry 
(1) GDK 7 LEP mine Singareni Collieries Company Limited: 
•   Large quantity of water, estimated to be several thousand gallons, had 
accumulated in panel No.3S/SS-IA in No.3 seam bottom sect ion which was 
extracted in the year 2000 by splitting as final operation in conjunction with 
hydraulic sand stowing. The accumulation was due to inter-granular space in 
sand, shrinkage of stowed sand with time, inadequate stowing. 

Written Answers to [23 AUG., 2007] Unstarred Questions    61 
• In an area, which was declared non-workable by the owner in 1999, development 
in 2 dip district in No.3 seam top section was started in April, 2003. 
• This 2 dip development district in No.3 seam top section was being worked 
within 60 metres of the No.3 seam bottom section workings in panel No.3S/SS-
lA. This work was done without taking prior permission from the Regional 
Inspector of Mines and without taking due precautions against the danger of 
inundation arising out of working close to water-logged workings. 
• The parting between top and bottom sections of 3 seam which was to be kept 
atleast 5 metres, got reduced by roof falls occurring in 3 seam bottom section 
along the 2 metres throw fault plane. The parting must have been reduced to a 
few centimeters just before the rupture. 
• The head of water, which was calculated to be about 15 metres, was enough to 
cause the rupture leading to sudden inrush in top section. 
• The water rushed along 18L through the puncture in the form of a  wall of a 
height of about 1 metre. After travelling southwards, it entered No.2 dip where 17 
workers who were working in and below 19L and who were drowned in the 
inrushing water. 
• Lack of supervision in mining in general and stowing of sand in particular.  
There is no system in place whereby after stowing any responsible officer 
would certify that stowing was proper and adequate before the district could be 
closed. 
(2) GDK 8A Incline of Singareni Collieries Company Limited: 
1. Extraction in panel No. 46B wa s started on 17th July, 2003, while extraction in  
adjoining panel No. 46A on the South Side, was still continuing. Panel No. 46A was  
sealed off on 30- 9-2003. Panel No. 44 on the dip side and panel No. 41 on the  
North side of panel No. 46B had been extracted long ago. 
2. If whole pillars are considered, then line of extraction was diagonal. However the 
permission under Reg.100 required diagonal line of faces i.e. faces in the line of extraction 
should have been diagonal. But as already mentioned earlier, one half pillar to the South -
east of the slice, where the accident occurred, had been extracted fully ahead of the 
diagonal line. Thus, in the truly diagonal line of face extraction, part of the load, which would 
have been borne by the half pillar, shifted to the rib at the site of accident. 
3. The first local fall occurred in night shift of 14.10.2003 followed by second one in 
night shift of 15.10.2003 and the third fall occurred on the night shift of 16.10.2003 causing 
the accident. The exposed area in the goal was 5160 sq. m at the time of accident. 
4. Code of practice for induced blasting to bring down the hanging goal should that 
exceed 4000 sq. m not followed in the sense that depth of shot holes had been reduced and 
also the additional shot holes for induced blasting parallel to the goal 

62     Written Answers to [RAJYASABHA] Unstarred Questions 
required to be made when the hanging goal are exceeded 4000 sq. m. were not completed 
in quick time. 
5. Reduction of rib also appeared to be more than what could be considered judicious 
for the situation. 
6. From the deposition before the Court and during the statutory inquiry by DGMS 
and also available records, it is apparent that there were indications of weighting in the 
working areas prior to the accident. Under the given ge o-mining condition, weighting 
followed by the floor heaving could be expected before the local falls and the main falls 
indicating redistribution of the stresses. Apparently. the management failed to read the 
indications correctly. 
7. Extraction in panel No 46B had been started while extraction in panel 46A on the south 
side was still in progress. This accident occurred only about 16/17 days after adjoining 
panel was sealed off. So it can be safely concluded that movement in panel No. 46A had 
not completely stopped at the time of accident. Load transfer due to interaction of the 
stresses from the adjoining goal probably led to the sudden dynamic loading for which 
the workers failed to get any early indication. 
8. In 2nd shift of 16-10-2003, 1st dip slice of 55-1/2 LS/9 Dip got connected to the goal 
on the dip side and the rib on the south side was reduced by blasting. At about 1.00 A.M on 
17-10-2003 (3rd shift of 16-10-2003). while loading of coal from the blasted rib was being 
done in the presence of some coal -cutters, support personnel and the sirdar, a local fall 
occurred in the goal which extended into the workings crushing the south side rib and ten 
persons were buried underneath it while two escaped with minor injuries.  
(3) Central Saunda mine accident of Cent ral Coalfields Limited on  
15-06-2005: 
The accident was caused due to connection between working district of Bansgarha 
seam and overlying water -logged abandoned workings of Hathidari seam caused by fall 
of roof. The accident occurred due to failure as keepi ng Hatidari seam (lying above and 
within 60m of working district of Bansgarha seam) free of water as required by condition 
number 5.3 of permission letter no. RR/10297/Perm-100(I)/03/2930 dated 20.11.03 granted 
under regulation 100 (I) of Coal Mine Regulation 1957. The scam was extracted beyond 
permitted area in panel no. II forming an exposure of fault plane constituted to the fall of 
roof and subsequently  inundation. 
(4) In case of Bhatdih (Nagda) Colliery of BCCL, the Court of Enquiry  
instituted is yet to submit its report.

Poor quality of services 
1237. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Will the Minister of  
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether TRAI has recently expressed its displeasure regarding poor quality of 
service provided by private service providers both in the fields of land line and mobile 
telephony; 
(b) if so, the specific areas where improvements are needed; and 

Written Answers to [23 AUG, 2007] Unstarred Questions     81 
(c) the action taken by TRAI to improve the services to the desired level? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MI NISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND 
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a) Yes, Sir. Recently Telecom 
Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), in meetings with the service providers, expressed 
its concern for the poor quality of service provided by them in respect of certain Quality of 
Service (QoS) parameters as prescribed in TRAI's regulation on QoS, both for Basic and 
Cellular Mobile Telephone Services. 
(b) As per the performance monitoring report submitted by the service  
providers to TRAI for quarter ending March 2007, the parameters where the  
improvement is needed in general are Provision of Telephones (New connection  
after registration of demand), Fault incidences, Mean Time to Repair, Call  
Completion Rate, Customer Care and Percentage of calls answered  by operator  
(voice to voice) for Basic Services. Whereas, in the case of Cellular Services, the 
parameter which need to be improved are Percentage of calls answered (voice to  
voice). 
(c) TRAI had earlier issued a Quality of Service (QoS) regulation in Jul y 2000  
and subsequently modified in July 2005 so as to benchmark various QoS  
parameters for basic and cellular mobile services. In the recently held meetings,  
TRAI has made it amply clear to the service providers that they must meet the  
quality of service parameters by improving the deficient areas. 
TRAI has been monitoring the performance of service providers against the benchmarks 
for various Quality of Service parameters through: 
(i)    quarterly performance monitoring reports; 
(ii)    monthly congestion reports on the parameter Point of Interconnection (POI) 
congestion; 
(iii)   independent agency to assess the Quality of Service provided by the services 
providers; and 
(iv)   periodical surveys by independent agency to assess the customer perception 
of service, against the Quality of Service benchmarks. 
TRAI has issued show cause notices on 06.03.2006 to six mobile operators, in whose 
network the number of POI having congestion above the prescribed benchmark has 
increased. These operators have since moved Telecom Dispute Settlement and Appellate 
Tribunal (TDSAT) against the show cause notices and the matter is sub-judice.

Statement 
Details of steps taken by Government to protect wild tiger 
The steps taken by the Government to protect wild tiger from, depletion are as below:- 
Legal steps 
1. Amendment of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 for providing  
enabling provisions for constitution of the National Tiger Conservation  
Authority and the Tiger and Other Endangered Species Crime Control  
Bureau. The punishment in cases of offence within a tiger reserve has  
been enhanced. The Act also provides for forfeiture of any equipment,  
vehicle or weapon that has been used for committing any  wild life  
offence. 
Administrative steps 
2. Strengthening of antipoaching activities, including special strategy for monsoon 
patrolling, by providing funding support to Tiger Reserve States, as proposed 
by them, for deployment of antipoaching squads involving ex-army 
personnel/home guards, apart from workforce comprising of local people, in 
addition to strengthening of communication/wireless facilities. 
3. Constitution of the" National Tiger Conservation Authority with effect from 
4.09.2006, for strengthening tiger conservation by, inter alia, ensuring 
normative standards in tiger reserve management, preparation of reserve specific 
tiger conservation plan, laying down annual/audit report before Parliament, 
constituting State level Steering Committees under the Chairmanship of Chief 
Ministers and establishment of Tiger Conservation Foundation. 
4. Constitution of a multidisciplinary Tiger and Other Endangered Species Crime 
Control Bureau (Wildlife Crime Control Bureau) with effect from 6.6.2007 
comprising of officers fr om Police, Forest, Customs and other enforcement 
agencies to effectively control illegal trade in wildlife. 
5. In principle approval accorded for declaring eight new Tiger Reserves. 
Financial steps 
6. Financial and technical help is provided to the States under various  
Centrally Sponsored Schemes, viz. Project Tiger and Development of  
National Parks and Sanctuaries for enhancing the capacity and  
infrastructure of the States for providing effective protection to wild  
animals.

International Cooperation 
7. India has a Memorandum of Understanding with Nepal on controlling trans-
boundary illegal trade in wildlife and conservation, apart from a protocol on 
tiger conservation with China. 
8. A Global Tiger Forum of Tiger Range Countries has been created for addressing 
international issues related to tiger conservation. 
9. During the 14th meeting of the Conference of Parties to CITES, which was held 
from 3rd to 15th June, 2007 at The Hague, India introduced a resolution along 
with China, Nepal and the Russian Federation, which contains directions to 
Parties with operations breeding tigers on a commercial scale, for restricting 
such captive populations to a level supportive only to conserving wild tigers.

intervention appealing to China to phase out tiger farming, and eliminate

1271. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to  
state:

Written Answers to [23 AUG, 2007] Unstarred Questions   109 
(d) by when Government are, likely to take steps to end pollution in Yamuna which has 
currently become a dirty drain and being misused? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS 
(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) and (b) According to the information received 
from the Ministry of Water Resources, there are proposals for construction of three storage 
reservoirs namely, Renuka Dam Project, Kishau Dam Project and Lakhwar Vyasi Dam 
Project, mainly intended for regulating the flow of water in the river Yamuna during the year 
by increasing the lean season flow after storing the excess water during high flow periods. In 
this regard, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed in May, 1994 by the Chief 
Ministers of basin states of Delhi, UP, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Rajasthan. The MoU 
covers allocation of annual utilizable flow of r iver Yamuna to the basin States including 
Uttarakhand. The storage projects namely, Renuka Dam (Government of Himachal Pradesh 
through Pabbar Valley Power Corporation), Kishau Dam (Government of Uttarakhand through 
Tehri Hydro Power Development Corporation) and Lakhwar Vyasi Dam (Government of 
Uttarakhand through National Hydro-electric Power Corporation) are at various stages of 
investigation/preparation of Detailed Project Report (DPR) and obtaining various clearances 
regarding Environment and Forest, Resettlement and Rehabilitation etc. 
(c) The provisional cost of the three storage dams is presently estimated to be Rs. 
12291 crore approximately. In the context of improvement of water quality in river 
Yamuna, the estimated cost of sewage treatment capacity env isaged to be 
created/augmented in Haryana, Delhi and U.P. under Yamuna Action Plan, Phase -II of 
Ministry of Environment and Forests is Rs. 173.03 crore. In addition, Government of NCT of 
Delhi has taken up large scale sewerage and sewage treatment works fr om its own plan 
funds. 
(d) The quality of water in Yamuna has not shown the desired improvement, particularly 
in Delhi, owing to the large gap between the demand and the availability of the sewage 
treatment capacity and lack of availability of fresh water for ensuring minimum flow in the 
river. Implementation of the river pollution abatement works is an ongoing and continuous 
activity of the Government under which various schemes of pollution abatement are 
implemented by the Government based upon the estimated pollution loads. Due to ever -
increasing population leading to increased pollution load and gap in the availability of 
financial resources to take up the works commensurate with the requirements, there is likely 
to be persistent divergence between the pollu tion load tackled and the actual pollution 
load. While the construction of reservoirs is mainly intended for regulating the flow of 
water during the year by increasing the lean season flow after storing the excess water 
during high flow periods, it will also help in ameliorating the water quality of river 
Yamuna. 
Receding Gangotri glacier 
1272. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether India's holiest river Ganga is under greater threat from warming than ever 
before as Himalayan source Gangotri glacier is receding by 120 feet a year and some of the 
glaciers could disappear by 2030; 

110   Written Answers to [RAJYASABHA] Unstarred Questions 
(b) whether UN findings/environmentalists want Indian Government to enforce 
strict reduction of greenhouse gas emission, primary cause of climate change, apart from 
asking corporations not to dump toxins in the river; and 
(c) if so remedial measures Government have taken so far in this regard as 50 crore 
people depend on Ganga river for spiritual ly purifying, drinking water and farming 
purposes? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND 
FORESTS (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) No, Sir. As per the studies carried out 
by Geological Survey of India (GSI) for the period 1935- 1996, Gangotri  Glacier is 
receding at an average rate of 18.8 m/yr. Studies carried out by other agencies have 
variously estimated the rate of recession as 17.15 m/yr during the period 1971- 2004 and 
12.10 m during the year 2005 -06. The catchment of Ganga and other river s originating 
from Himalaya happen to be located on a high rainfall zone, and are thus fed by 
substantial amount of rainwater too. It is a fact that Himalayan glaciers are receding. GSI 
is monitoring the Himalayan glaciers and making an effort to understan d the causes of 
recession. It has not been established conclusively that recession is only due to global 
warming. It may also be a cyclic phase of recession witnessed in the history of evolution 
of the earth. 
(b) The UN Framework Convention on Climate Chan ge recognises the fact that as 
developing countries grow these emissions are bound to increase. 
Although India as a developing country does not have any mitigation commitments, 
we are following a sustainable development path through range of policies and 
programmes to mitigate climate change, some of which are: 
I.     ensuring energy conservation and improved energy efficiency in various 
sectors as well as setting up of Bureau of Energy Efficiency 
II. promoting use of renewable energy 
III. power sector reforms and active renewable energy programme 
IV use of cleaner and lesser carbon intensive fuel for transport 
V fuel switching to encourage cleaner energy 
VL afforestation and conservation of forests 
VII. promotion of clean coal technologies 
VIII. reduction of gas flaring 
IX. encouraging Mass Rapid Transport systems 
X. environmental quality management for all sectors 
As per Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 and Environment (Protection) Act, 
1986 along with rules under these Acts, corporations can not dump toxins into the river. This law is 
enforced by State Pollution Control Boards.

Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of National River Conservation Plan of the 
Ministry of Environme nt and Forests, various works are undertaken for pollution 
abatement in major rivers including Ganga through interception and diversion of sewage 
for its treatment and construction of Sewage Treatment Plants and Low Cost Sanitation. 
Under the Ganga Action Plan-(GAP) Phase I & II, 1747 mld. (million litres per day) of 
sewage treatment capacity has been created so far. With the pollution abatement works 
completed so far under Ganga Action Plan, the water quality of the river Ganga has shown 
discernible improv ement at major locations over its pre -GAP quality as per the water 
quality monitoring undertaken by independent reputed institutions in the country. The 
National Environment Policy, 2006 also advocates an integrated approach for management 
of river basins by the concerned river authorities, ensuring maintenance of adequate 
flows, adherence to water quality standards throughout their course in all seasons and

Abolition of manual scavenging 
†1289. SHRI SURENDRA LATH: W ill the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN 
POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of the fact that scavenging is still -prevalent in 
various States of the country; 
(b) the number of persons convicted or penalty imposed against them so far under the 
Employment of Manual Scavengers and Construction of Dry Latrines (Prohibition) Act, 
1993; and 
(c) whether Government have any such information that how many persons are still 
engaged in this inhuman work in different States of the country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN 
POVERTY ALLEVIATION (KUMARI SELJA) (a) Yes, Sir. Manual Scavenging still  exists 
in some parts of the country. 
(b) and (c) In order to stop the practice of manual scavenging the Parliament has 
enacted Employment of Manual Scavengers and Construction of Dry Latrines (Prohibition) 
Act, 1993 which provides for penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act. 
This Act has been adopted by the States of Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, 
Gujarat, Goa, Haryana, Jharkhand, Kamataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Meghalaya, 
Orissa, Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Tripura, Uttaranchal, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal. J&K has 
not adopted this act as so far. States of Arunachal Pradesh, Kerala, Manipur, Mizoram, 
Nagaland and Sikkim have not adopted the act but have stated that there are no dry latrines. 
States of Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh have their own legislation on the subject. Details 
of prosecutions which come under the purview of the respective State Governments are, 
however, not maintained in this Ministry. The Government of India implements a Self 
Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers (SRMS) which aims at 
rehabilitation of manual scavengers who at any point of time, were engaged in m anual 
scavenging and are yet to be assisted for rehabilitation. As per the scheme, there were 3,42,468 
such persons, which included their dependents also.

of Phase-V. The design, development and delivery of the Phase-III programme was entrusted 
jointly to TERI School of Advanced Studies, New Delhi and Duke Centre for 
International Development, Duke University, USA, that of the Phase-IV programme was 
entrusted jointly to Indian Institute of Management, Bangalore and Maxwell School, Syracuse 
University, USA and that of the Phase- V programme was entrusted jointly to Indian Institute 
of Management, Ahmedabad and Kennedy School of Government, Harvard University, USA. 
The participants of Phase-Ill & IV are being trained for 6 weeks in India and are being sent 
to USA and to an Asian Country respectively, for a 2 -week exposure visit. The officers 
participating in the Phase - V programme are being trained at Indian Institute of 
Management, Ahmedabad for all the 4 weeks. 
In addition to the above mandatory mid career training, every IAS officer is required to 
attend a 1 week in -service training programme in a block of 2 years. Such training is 
imparted in various leading institutions within the country having specialization in particular 
sectors or skills, in order to update the knowledge and skills of the officers in selected 
subjects. 
The IAS officers, who have a minimum of 10 years of experience, are also eligible to 
attend one more flexible training programme once in a financial year at the Indian Institutes 
of Management located at Bangalore, Ahmedabad, Calcutta and Lucknow.

Employment on the basis of false caste certificate 
1300. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether a number o f persons have secured employment in Government 
offices/departments and public sector undertakings on the basis of false caste certificates; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the action taken in the matter; and 
(c) what measure have been taken to prevent securing employment on false caste 
certificates? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC 
GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRI SURESH PACHOURI): (a) and (b) The CBI has 
registered 34 cases for securing jobs on the basis of fake ST certificates. Out of t hese 34 
cases, charge sheets have been filed in 22 cases and 9 cases have been closed for want of 
evidence. In one case, regular departmental action for major penalty has been 
recommended and the investigation has not been completed in the remaining 2 cases.  
As regards securing jobs on the basis of fake SC certificate the CBI has registered 2 
cases against 3 persons. Out of these charge sheet has been filed in one case and the 
remaining case is under investigation. 
(c) The Government has issued instruction from time to time that it is mandatory on 
the part of the appointing authority to verify the caste status of SC/ ST/OBC officials at the 
time of initial appointment. These instructions have been reiterated vide O.M. No. 
36022/1/2007-Estt. (Res) dated 20.03.2007.

Percentage of reservation 
1302. SHR1 PRAVEEN RASHTRAPAL: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) the percentage of res ervation for SC and ST in the direct recruitment posts for 
Group A,B,C and D in the vacancies of Central Government establishments; 
(b) when were these percentages fixed and by whom; and 
(c) the reasons for not revising these percentages on the basis of census figures? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC 
GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHR1 SURESH PACHOURI): (a) In case of direct 
recruitment on all India basis by open competition, reservation to the Scheduled Castes and 
Scheduled Tribes is available at the rate of 15% and 7.5% respectively. In case of direct 
recruitment on all India basis, otherwise than by open competition, reservation to them is 
available at the rate of 16.66% and 7.5% respectively. In case of direct recruitment to 
Group C & D posts, normally attracting candidates from a locality or a region, reservation 
for SCs and STs is generally determined keeping in view the proportion of their population 
in the respective States/UTs. 
(b) Present rate of reservation for SCs in case of direct recrui tment on all India basis 
otherwise than by open competition was fixed in September, 1947 and current rates of 
reservation for SCs in case of direct recruitment by open competition and for STs in case of 
direct recruitment on all India basis by open competition as well as otherwise than by open 
competition were fixed in March, 1970. Quantum of reservation in case of direct 
recruitment to Group C and D posts on local or regional basis has been revised with 
effect from 5.7.2005. 
(c) Quantum of reservation in case of direct recruitment to Group C and D posts, 
normally attracting candidates from a locality or a region is generally revised keeping in view 
the proportion of their population as per the 2001 Census. The Supreme Court has held that 
the Constitution enables the State to make provisions for adequate representation and not 
proportionate representation to backward classes in services. It has also held that total 
reservation for SCs, STs and Other Backward Classes should not exceed the limit of 50%. In 
case of direct recruitment on all India basis, reservation for the Scheduled Castes, 
Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes is already either 49.5% or 50%. Therefore, it 
has not been found possible to revise the quantum of reservation on the basis of census 
figures.

Killing of Tamils in Sri Lanka 
1306. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the International independent group of eminent persons 
has opined that in the name of tackling terrorism, innocent Tamil civilian population in Sri 
Lanka is mercilessly killed indiscriminately by the Sri Lankan Government leading to heavy 
flow of refugees exceeding one lakh on Indian Soil; 
(b) if so, the action taken by Government of India to mitig ate this problem and save 
from killing of innocent Tamil civilians; and 
(c) whether it is also a fact that the measures taken in terms of infrastructure, food, 
shelter, employment, other facilities, livelihood are wanting and inadequate to rehabilitate the 
refugees coming to India? 
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE): (a) No. 
(b) There have been hostilities between the Sri Lankan armed forces and the LTTE 
since the beginning of 2006, which have resulted in serious loss of lives including that of 
Tamil civilians and in an increase in Sri Lankan Tamil refugees entering India. While 
conveying our concern on this issue, we have emphasised to the Government of Sri Lanka 
that the only solution to the ethnic problem is a negotiated political settlement acceptable 
to all communities in Sri Lanka. 
(c) Government are taking all necessary measures for the rehabilitation of Sri 
Lankan Tamil refugees entering India. We have stressed to the Government of Sri Lanka 
the need to create conditions for the safe and voluntary return of refugees to their homes.

Changes in working of MMD 
1316. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA: Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD 
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) the targets set by Government for 2007- 08 to bring in changes in the way the 
Mercantile Marine Department (MMD) functions under D.G. Shipping;  
(b) whether minor changes have been proposed to reduce delays and whimsical 
demands of surveyors; 
(c) how many ports have MMD offices to do surveys; 
(d) the safeguards that would be instituted to reduce arbitrar iness, delays,  
needless demands, expensive surveys and harassment for small companies and  
people; and 

Written Answers to [23 AUG, 2007] Unstarred Questions   151 
(e) the reasons for not bringing about any changes in MMD to develop shipping and 
maritime sector? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS (SHRI 
T.R. BAALU): (a) to (e) There are 5 Regional level Mercantile Marine Department 
(MMD) offices and 13 District level MMD offices including newly created Regional 
offices at Kochi and Kandla a nd 3 District level offices of MMD at Paradip, New 
Mangalore and Haldia which have been set up in January, 2006 covering all the major 
ports in the country. The Mercantile Marine Departments administer various Merchant 
Shipping Laws and Rules under Merchan t Shipping Act, 1958 and IMO conventions 
including survey and inspection of ships. With a view to modernizing and streamlining 
the functioning of the Mercantile Marine Departments and also ensuring efficiency and 
transparency, Government have taken the following steps: 
(i)    A Citizen Charter providing the details of various functions and target 
periods within which various services are to be rendered to the shipping 
industry without causing any inconvenience and delay has been made 
available at all mercan tile marine Departments and on the website of 
Directorate General of Shipping. 
(ii)    A number of surveys and inspections have been assigned to recognize 
classification societies vide this Department's notification published in the 
Gazette of India-Extraordinary S.O. No.640(E) dated 27th May, 2004. 
(iii)     A redressal mechanism has been set up to look into the genuine 
complaints of the shipping industry. The Merchant Shipping Act, 1958 
has provisions for appeals by shipping companies against unsatisfactory 
surveys and inspections. Such appeals can be made in the Indian ports as 
well as abroad. 
(iv)   With the introduction of an e -Governance programme for the Mercantile 
Marine Department, Mumbai, Directorate General of Shipping and allied 
offices, most of the facilitative and regulatory approvals can be applied 
online by intending enterprises. Further, an online redressal system has 
also been introduced in order to reduce delays in the disposal of 
complaints. 
(v)    A quality management system with the obje ctive of providing quick and 
timely service to the shipping industry has been introduced in the 
Directorate General of Shipping. 
In addition to above, the Right to Information Act has been implemented in letter 
and spirit thereby ensuring greater transparency to public. There is a well laid down 
redressal mechanism which includes on line submission of grievances directly to the 
Directorate General of Shipping. Customer friendly forms have been developed and are 
available on the website. Most of the services  can be availed by online submission of 
forms.

Crisis of safe drinking water 
1324.   SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI: 
SHRI SANJAY RAUT: 
Will the Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the country is facing serious crisis of safe drinking water; 
(b) whether Government have formulated any national policy to this effect; 
(c) the details of steps taken or proposed to be taken for tackling serious crisis of safe 
drinking water in the country, particularly in Maharashtra State; 
(d) whether Government are considering to change water purification method through 
Chlorine as it sometimes causes serious health problems in the country; and 
(e) the details of healthy and cost effective water purification being used by the developed 
nations and Government's response/reaction thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT (SHRI 
AJAY MAKEN): (a) to (c) Supply pf drinking water is a State subject. The Ministry has not 
received any information from the State Governments about serious crisis in availability 
of safe drinking water in the urban areas of the country. 

Written Answers to [23 AUG, 2007] Unstarred Questions   157 
The drinking water has been assigned first allocation priority in planning & operation 
of system in the National Water Policy, 2002 announced by the Government of India.  
However, in order to improve drinking water supply and mitigate water supply shortage in 
the urban areas, Govt. of India has launched two new initiatives i.e. Urban Infrastructure 
and Governance and Urban Infrastructure Development Scheme for Small & Medium 
Towns (UIDSSMT) under Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission in December, 
2005 under which financial assistance is provided to all the State Governments and UT 
Administration as per guidelines provide infrastructure facilities including water supply. 
Details of projects approved under these Schemes for State of Maharashtra are given in 
Statement-I and II respectively (See below). Under Accelerated Urban Water Supply 
Programme (AUWSP) 37 projects were approved for State of Maharashtra and full 
Central share of Rs. 5789.12 lakh has been released. This scheme has been subsumed in 
UIDSSMT w.e.f. December, 2005. 
(d) At present there is no p roposal with Government of India to switch over to any 
other methods of purification/disinfection. 
(e) In developing countries, the treated water for domestic consumption is disinfected 
through chlorination/ozonation/UV radiation process and supplied on contin uous basis. 
Though Ozonation and UV radiation process are effective in disinfecting the water but it is 
more costly compared to chlorination. Chlorination is safer for intermittent water supply 
system, which is prevailing in the country. It also helps maintain 'residual effect' as there may 
be possibility of contamination of water in distribution lines during non-supply hours.

during construction, road safety audit on selected stretches, have been 
undertaken by National Highways Authority of India.

(iv)   Involvement of NGOs for road safety activities by Department of Road Transport 
and Highways and National Highways Authority of India. 
(v)    Setting up of Model Driving Training School in the country. 
(vi)  Publicity campaign on road safety awareness through audio- visual-print 
media. 
(vii) Institution of National Award for voluntary organizations/individual for 
outstanding work in the field of road safety. 
(viii) Tightening of safety standards of vehicles. 
(ix)  Provision of cranes and ambulances to various State Governments/ NGOs 
under National Highway Accident Relief Service Scheme. National 
Highways Authority of India also provides ambulances at a distance of 50 
Km. on each of its completed highways under its Operation and 
Maintenance contracts.

Gandhinagar under JNNURM 
1342.  SHRI KANJIBHAI PATEL: 
SHRI KESHUBHAI S. PATEL: 
Will the Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the time when Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) was 
launched in the country; 
(b) the salient features of the mission; 
(c) whether it is a fact that all the capital cities of other States are included in the 
JNNURM except Gandhinagar, the Capital of Gujarat; and 
(d) if so, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT (SHRI 
AJAY MAKEN): (a) and (b) The Government of India launched Jawaharlal Nehru National 
Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) on 3rd December, 2005 aiming at reforms driven, fast 
track, planned development of identified cities with focus on efficiency in urban 
infrastructure/services delivery mechanism, community participation and accountability of 
Urban Local Bodies (ULBsVParastatals towards citizen. A sum of Rs. 50,000 crore has been 
committed as Additional Central Assistance from Government of India under JNNURM for 
its two sub-missions, namely, Urban Infrastructure & Governance (Sub-Mission-I) and Basic 
Services for the Urban Poor (Sub~Mission-II) and two omnibus schemes, namely, Urban 
Infrastructure- Development Scheme for Small and Medium Towns (UIDSSMT) and integrated 
Housing and Slum Development Programme (IHSDP). The Mission is for a period of seven 
years beginning from 2005-06. 
(c) and (d) Yes, Sir. Decision to keep number of cities covered under JNNURM around 60 
was taken with the approval of Government. However, cities which are not covered, under 
Sub-Mission-I Urban Infrastructure and Governance of the JNNURM have been covered 
under UIDSSMT of JNNURM.

(a) whether it is a fact that as per DDA rules, no person can own two properties in 
Delhi; 
(b) if so, whether DDA follows the rules for everyone or for the poor/middle class 
residents only; 

186   Written Answers to [RAJYASABHA] Unstarred Questions 
(c) whether no action is beipg taken against influential people who have more than one 
property in Delhi; 
(d) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(e) the number of VIPs and top influential people owning more than one flat/ plot in 
Delhi? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN. THE MINISTRY OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT (SHRI 
AJAY MAKEN): (a) Delhi Development Authority (DDA) has reported that the allotment of 
plots is governed by the DDA (Disposal of Development Nazul Land) Rules, 1981 [Nazul 
Rules]. As per these rules, no residential plot shall be allotted to the persons who or whose 
wife/husband or any of his/her dependent children whether minor or not, or any of his/her 
dependent parents or dependent minor brothers or siste rs, ordinarily residing with such 
individual, own in full or in part, on lease or free-hold basis, any residential land or house, 
or who has been allotted on hire purchase basis any residential land or house in the Union 
Territory of Delhi. Provided that where, on the date of allotment. 
(0     the other land/flat owned by or allotted to such individual is less than 67 
sq.m., or 
(ii)   the house owned by such individual is on a plot of land which measures less 
than 67 sq.m., or 
(iii)   the share of such individual in any such other land or house measures less 
than 67 sq.m., 
he may be allotted a plot/flat in accordance with the provisions of the above said 
rules. 
In respect of allotment of residential plots under .the Rohini Residential Scheme of DDA, 
which was launched prior to the notification of Nazul Rules, while the eligibility conditions 
are same as in the Nazul Rules, the applicant was/is eligible to apply/get a plot under the 
scheme, if the individual share of the applicant in the jointly owned plot or land  under the 
residential house whose area is less than 65 sq.mtrs. However, persons who own a house or 
a plot allotted by the DDA on an area of even less than 65 sq.mtrs., are not eligible to get 
the residential plot. 
DDA has further reported that the allotment of flats is governed by the DDA (Management 
and Disposal of Housing Estates) Regulations, 1968. Under these regulations, while the 
eligibility conditions are same as in the Nazul Rules, a person is eligible to apply under the 
housing scheme if the  individual share of the applicant in the jointly owned plot or land 
under the residential house is less than 75 sq.yds. However, persons who own a house or 
a plot, allotted by the DDA, on an area of even less than 75 sq.yds., are not eligible to 
apply for allotment of DDA flats. 
However, any person after allotment from DDA can acquire more than one property 
by purchasing it from open market. 
(b) to (d) DDA follows the above rules for everyone. In order to adhere to these rules 
necessary affidavit about ownership of residential property is taken 

Written Answers to [23 AUG, 2007] Unstarred Questions   187 
from the allottees. If the violation of above rules is noticed, action as per terms and conditions 
of allotment is taken against the allottee, including cancellation of allotment. 
(e) The DDA has reported, that no such records are maintained by them.
